title: 3 ways the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 is actually worse than last year’s chip

body: Qualcomm is talking a big AI game with two flagship chipsets this year, the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 and Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 . But a closer look at the differences between these two chips reveals that the Extreme nomenclature is doing quite a lot of heavy lifting. Rather, it might be more realistic to call the regular version of the chip the 8 Elite Lite Gen 6. While the two flagship processors share the same 5GHz peak clock speeds, new GPU architecture, and many of the same new AI features, the “regular” version of the Gen 6 misses out on a few of Qualcomm’s most impressive technologies. The list includes cutting-edge video codecs, Matrix cores for AI graphics, and 50% more local memory to support on-device AI models.

body: Spacecraft propulsion traditionally relies on volatile fuels and separate, bulky systems for different types of maneuvering in space. NASA is working to change that paradigm. Engineers at NASA’s Marshall Space Flight Center in Huntsville, Alabama, recently completed a rigorous series of environmental and physical tests on a new small satellite designed to make spaceflight safer and more efficient. The ASCENT (Advanced Spacecraft Energetic Non-Toxic) Propulsion Dual Mode mission is a flight demonstration of a spacecraft about the size of a large shoebox. The mission will test a single, integrated propulsion system that uses a common fuel tank to feed two different types of engines. Dr. Nehemiah Williams, the demonstration’s project manager at NASA, prepares to start testing the mission’s flight hardware in a clean room at NASA’s Marshall Space Flight Center in Huntsville, Alabama. The mission will demonstrate a single, non-toxic propulsion system that combines both high-thrust and low-thrust capabilities into a common tank. body: TL;DR Google Messages is widely rolling out its redesigned long-press menu to stable users. The floating menu puts common message actions closer to your thumb and supports selective text copying. The features were previously made available to beta users in August, but the stable rollout still appears to be server-side. Long-pressing a message should be one of those tiny interactions you never have to think about. In Google Messages, though, it has long meant reaching toward the top of the screen for basic actions — hardly ideal when phones keep getting bigger. Google began cleaning that up months ago when it widened access to its redesigned menu in beta in August, and now the upgrade finally appears to be making the jump to stable users. Reddit user Lazy_Excitement_2602 spotted the new menu on the stable version of Google Messages, specifically version 20260903_04. Several other users in the thread also confirmed seeing it outside the beta program, including on a Samsung Galaxy S23 Plus and S25 Ultra, suggesting the rollout is no longer limited to Pixel devices or testers.

title: Here’s what Magic Pointer processes on your Googlebook — and what goes online
summary: Screen recognition stays local until you ask Gemini to act.
body: TL;DR Magic Pointer identifies things you can interact with on your Googlebook screen locally after you activate it. Once you select something and ask Gemini to act on it, it sends the content to a cloud model. Google says the AI cursor stays inactive until you deliberately trigger it. Google looked at one of the oldest parts of the desktop experience — the mouse cursor — and decided Gemini could make it useful for more than clicking things. The result is Magic Pointer, which can understand whatever you highlight on a Googlebook and help you act on it. That sounds incredibly handy, but it also raises a pretty important privacy question: when exactly does what’s on your screen leave your laptop and head to Google’s cloud? Google has now explained where that line sits. Speaking on Android Faithful , Alexander Kuscher, Google’s Senior Director of Product for Laptops and Tablets, broke down what happens behind the scenes when you use Magic Pointer.

body: TL;DR The ARMSX3 PS3 emulator just got a major update that fixes game crashes and adds several features. When the team behind the popular PS2 emulator ARMSX2 launched its PS3 emulator , it was just a proof of concept. As such, it had several issues, including the fact that most games didn’t run at a playable frame rate. Now, the devs have released an update that brings several improvements, including useful tweaks to touch controls. The update was announced in a Reddit post detailing a laundry list of improvements to the emulator. ARMSX3 now supports PS3 themes as library backgrounds. Users can set up pictures, slideshows, animated themes, and full 3D scenes that play live in the library background. According to the devs, they tested the feature with 92 dynamic themes, and each one played properly.

If you need help trying to find shops, restaurants, museums, or other locations around you, the search function in Google Maps can often come in handy. title: Your Pixel Watch now flags your risk of hypertension and diabetes
summary: Pixel Watch's new Health Guardian feature brings BP, insulin resistance, and sleep quality trends.
body: Credit: Joe Maring / Android Authority TL;DR Pixel Watch 3 and newer models are receiving the promised Health Guardian features. These include blood pressure and insulin resistance trends, as well as sleep quality analysis. The features are now available for free on the Pixel Watch, while Fitbit Air users will have to pay for them. At the launch of the Pixel Watch 5 , Google announced Health Guardian , a suite of features that detect trends from your health data and predict concerning physiologic changes, such as hypertension, diabetes, or sleep apnea. Google promised to roll it out “in fall,” and it’s now delivering on that commitment. Starting today, three vital Health Guardian features, including blood pressure trends, insulin resistance trends, and sleep breathing quality, are now available for the Pixel Watch 3 and Watch 4, alongside the newly launched Pixel Watch 5. These three metrics join Breathing Emergency detection , which has been available on the Pixel Watch 4 and 5 since launch, but only in limited European countries.

title: Gmail is turning its stars and importance markers blue, and users aren’t happy
summary: Google says the change helps with accessibility, but users complain it flattens hierarchy and clutters the inbox.
body: Credit: Joe Maring / Android Authority TL;DR Google replaced Gmail’s default yellow stars and yellow importance chevrons with high-contrast, saturated blue markers to improve accessibility. However, users complain that the identical blue tones flatten the visual hierarchy, make email scanning harder, and add visual clutter. While there’s no way to revert the changes, you can manually select a yellow star preset (and re-star items) or hide importance chevrons entirely in Settings. Google is rolling out a visual overhaul to Gmail on the web, replacing its longstanding yellow stars and importance markers with a bright, high-contrast blue. While Gmail has gained plenty of genuinely practical upgrades recently, such as letting you copy 2FA codes directly without opening emails or leveraging AI overview search capabilities , this particular color switch has annoyed desktop users who rely on quick visual cues to scan their messages. In a post on X , the official Gmail team confirmed the change, explaining that it updated the default star and “Important” label colors from yellow to blue to meet modern accessibility standards and ensure inboxes are easier to read and more inclusive.

title: Spotify just gave Meta Muse the keys to your music
summary: Your listening can now react to your plans without you lifting a finger.
body: TL;DR Spotify now works with Meta Muse, letting users control playback, find content, save tracks, and build playlists through conversation. Muse can also use context from calendars and schedules to automatically start the right music or podcast at the right time. Spotify is the first major music-streaming service to join Muse, which already connects with a growing list of third-party apps and services. Two weeks ago, Meta’s Muse arrived asking for the keys to your digital life. The personal AI agent can already work across email, calendars, payments, health apps, and shopping, and Meta is also bringing it to its smart glasses . Now Muse wants the aux cord, too. Spotify has announced a new integration that lets the agent control your listening and do more than simply press play. Once you connect Spotify to Muse, you can ask the agent to play music, podcasts, or audiobooks; save tracks to your Library; find something new; and build or edit playlists through conversation. Muse can also create Spotify’s Personal Podcasts from your notes and briefings.

title: The Pixel 11 is a bigger upgrade than I expected, but it still left me wanting more
summary: The software is better than ever, but the Pixel 11's hardware still disappoints me.
body: As soon as I picked up the Google Pixel 11 for the first time, I knew I wanted to love it. The slimmer, all-glass camera bar spoke to me as the perfect blend between the Pixel 10a’s flat back and the Pixel 11 Pro’s thicker camera housing. My favorite Android 17 perks, like the Pixel-exclusive Magic Capture and Creator Suite, still made the cut for Google’s cheapest flagship. And the missing features aren’t significant enough to notice they’re gone on the $899 Pixel 11. Unfortunately, after actually getting my hands on one, I found the Pixel 11 hard to love. The Tensor G6 chip isn’t the upgrade I hoped for , and without the vapor chamber found on the Pro phones, the Pixel 11 does genuinely overheat and stutter in everyday use. It’s harder than ever to choose between the Pixel 11 and, say, the Samsung Galaxy S26. I’ve tested both, and they each come with brutal compromises I’d rather not make.
